newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Foreign investment in Nigerian bourse up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Nigerian bourse up in 1996.

text.p: Foreigners bought shares worth $32.98 million in the Nigerian stock market in 1996, bourse chief executive Hayford Alile said on Friday.
He said this was a remarkable improvement over the $1.137 million recorded in 1995 when the market was thrown open to foreign investors.
Details of where the portfolio investors came from were not immediately available but Alile said the trend should continue this year.
He said officials of the exchange had travelled abroad to promote the Nigerian market in 1996, and their efforts had increased foreign awareness of the exchange.
"It is expected that the trend will continue in a much more dramatic manner in 1997," Alile said.
The Nigerian military government in 1995 opened the exchange to foreigners by abrogating two laws which barred transfer of funds abroad and curtailed foreign equity holding in Nigerian businesses.

Analysts said foreign capital inflow would have been higher but for Nigeria's protracted political logjam and its face-off with many Western nations over human rights and slow pace of democratisation.
The country plunged into crisis in 1993 when the military rulers annulled a presidential election that would have restored democracy to Africa's most populous nation.

The presumed winner of that poll, wealthy businessman Moshood Abiola, has been detained since June 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of military ruler General Sani Abacha, who has promised to hand over after a new poll in 1998.
